decisive_items: Total occlusion at the ostium of the left anterior descending coronary artery
T-waves became upright in V2 to V4
Deeply inverted T-waves in leads V2 to V4
response.rationale: Dynamic T-wave pseudonormalization with total LAD occlusion and normal troponin indicates acute coronary syndrome, likely unstable angina, rather than variant angina or myocardial infarction with necrosis.

rejected.why: Hypertension and elevated blood pressure alone do not explain the acute chest pain, dynamic ECG changes, or LAD occlusion.
Variant angina typically causes rest pain with transient ST elevation and vasospasm, whereas this pain is exertional with fixed total LAD occlusion.
Total occlusion is present, but normal troponin and absence of ST elevation do not support myocardial infarction with necrosis.
Coronary artery disease is the underlying substrate, but the acute presentation and dynamic ECG changes make acute coronary syndrome the more precise diagnosis.
